newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Poland sees change by Moscow over NATO expansion.
newsitem.headline: Poland sees change by Moscow over NATO expansion.

text.p: Poland, one of Moscow's former allies and a leading candidate to join NATO, said on Friday it believed Russia now accepted that the alliance's eastwards expansion was inevitable.

Foreign Minister Dariusz Rosati and Minister of State for Defence Andrzej Karkoszka told reporters they saw an evolution in Moscow's previous outright opposition to a position where it wanted to use the issue to win concessions from the West.

"They are preparing themselves for NATO enlargement...Their aim to is to get concessions in other areas," Rosati told reporters after a two-day visit to Brussels to push Poland's case for swift European Union and NATO membership.

Rosati said he did not think the change, underlined by a visit to Brussels this week by Russian security supremo Alexander Lebed, would result in a slowing-down of the alliance's expansion into former communist Europe.
"NATO enlargement is well on track," he said, adding that he expected countries to be invited to start membership talks at a special heads of government summit next summer.
Korkoszka said Lebed, who toured NATO's political and military headquarters, came to Brussels "like a tiger and left like a pussycat."

He said Poland was working on a range of areas, from continuing democratisation of its Defence Ministry and English lessons for officers to changes to its accounting system, to make NATO membership more easily attainable.
